bug_description.original: Stack-buffer-overflow in ot::Cli::Utils::OutputLine OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=411460530 ``` Crash type: Stack-buffer-overflow READ {*} Crash state: ot::Cli::Utils::OutputLine ot::Cli::Dns::HandleDnsRecordResponse ot::Dns::Client::FinalizeQuery ```
bug_description.normalized: The staged CLI testcase issues a `dns query 3` command whose first label is 7 bytes long and whose remaining dot-separated labels are 62, 63, 59, and 59 bytes long, all filled with `0xff`. OpenThread stores that combined query name and later re-expands it in `Dns::HandleDnsRecordResponse` into local buffer `char name[OT_DNS_MAX_NAME_SIZE]`. `Name::ReadName` can write the trailing dot for this 255-character textual name but has no byte left for the terminating NUL, so `otDnsRecordResponseGetQueryName` returns `kErrorNoBufs` with `name` left unterminated. `HandleDnsRecordResponse` ignores that failure and immediately prints `name` with `OutputLine("DNS query response for %s ", name)`, so the formatting path reads past the end of the stack buffer until it finds a later NUL byte. The saved ASan layout shows the first invalid read starts immediately after `name`, grounding this witness in the unchecked query-name extraction path.

source.code:
SuccessOrExit(error = otDnsClientQueryRecord(GetInstancePtr(), recordType, aArgs[1].GetCString(),
                                                 aArgs[2].GetCString(), &HandleDnsRecordResponse, this, config));
source.description: First project-side statement that consumes the attacker-controlled CLI tokens as DNS name components and creates the query object later reread by the crashing callback.
source.value_from: The 266-byte staged `poc` is a CLI line `dns query 3 <first-label> <next-labels>` passed through `otCliInputLine()`. The `record-type` token is `3`, the first label is 7 raw `0xff` bytes, and the `next-labels` token is four dot-separated raw-byte labels of lengths 62, 63, 59, and 59.

root_cause.description: The callback discards the `kErrorNoBufs` result from query-name extraction and treats `name` as a valid C string even when the 255-byte stack buffer could not be null-terminated.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this line to `SuccessOrExit(error = otDnsRecordResponseGetQueryName(...))`, matching the missing obligation on the witnessed path.

sink.description: Final crashing read. Variadic formatting consumes `%s` for the unterminated `name` buffer and continues reading beyond the end of that stack array.
sink.note: ASan reports a `READ of size 256` at the byte immediately after `name[255]` in `HandleDnsRecordResponse`, which matches `%s` scanning across adjacent stack slots until a later NUL is found.

parser_admitted.description: The staged CLI line is admitted as a DNS arbitrary-record query because it provides the required non-empty `next-labels` token after `dns query 3 <first-label>`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call transfers the attacker-controlled label bytes into DNS client query construction, where they become the oversized textual query name later copied back into `name[255]`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The stored name decodes to 254 visible characters before `ReadName()` appends its mandatory trailing dot, so its valid C-string form needs 256 bytes including the NUL terminator.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer copies the staged bytes into a NUL-terminated CLI line and feeds them to `otCliInputLine()`.
CLI DNS query parsing accepts the `dns query 3 ...` command and submits the attacker-controlled first label and remaining labels to the DNS client as an arbitrary-record query.
The DNS client stores the supplied labels in the query message and later dispatches the resulting record response back to the CLI callback.
Query-name extraction into `name[255]` fails with `kErrorNoBufs`, but the callback ignores that failure and still passes `name` to `OutputLine("%s")`.
Variadic formatting scans past the end of the unterminated stack buffer, causing the recorded ASan stack-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The harness turns the staged 266-byte testcase into one NUL-terminated CLI command line and hands it to OpenThread's CLI parser. This is the unscored entry boundary, not the scored source.

Source. The project parser accepts the command as `recordType == 3` with a 7-byte first label and a `next-labels` token split into four labels of lengths 62, 63, 59, and 59. Those raw bytes now become the DNS query name carried into the client.
The DNS client copies the attacker-controlled first label from step 1 into the stored query message as the leading name label.

The client appends the remaining dot-separated labels and terminator. Together with step 2, the stored query decodes back to 254 visible characters before `ReadName()` adds its mandatory trailing dot, so a successful C-string reconstruction would need 256 bytes including NUL.
When the DNS client finalizes this response as an arbitrary-record query, it dispatches the callback with `aResponse` still referencing the query message populated in steps 2 and 3.

While reconstructing the query name into `char name[255]`, `ReadName()` can store the trailing dot for this maximal textual name but then has no byte left for the NUL terminator. It therefore returns `kErrorNoBufs` after leaving `name` without a terminator.

Root cause. The callback discards the `kErrorNoBufs` result from step 5 instead of stopping or reporting failure, so `name` remains a 255-byte unterminated stack buffer that still gets treated as a C string.
The unterminated stack buffer from step 6 is passed as a `%s` argument before the later `SuccessOrExit(aError)` check at line 719, so the unsafe print is reached on the witnessed path.

Sink. Formatting consumes the `%s` argument from step 7 and keeps reading past `name[255]` until a later NUL byte in adjacent stack storage, which matches ASan's report that the first invalid byte is immediately after local array `name` in `HandleDnsRecordResponse`.

format.name: OpenThread CLI dns query line
format.contract: The file must be a single CLI command `dns query 3 <first-label> <next-labels>` where `<first-label>` is exactly 7 raw `0xff` bytes and `<next-labels>` is exactly four dot-separated raw-byte labels of lengths 62, 63, 59, and 59. That exact label layout reconstructs to a 255-character textual DNS name after `ReadName()` adds the trailing dot, which makes `otDnsRecordResponseGetQueryName(..., name, 255)` fail with no room left for the NUL terminator.
